1. Why is the sky blue?
- Sunlight contains all colors of visible light (white light)
- When sunlight enters the atmosphere, it interacts with gas molecules
- Rayleigh scattering occurs when light interacts with particles much smaller than the wavelength of light
- Rayleigh scattering is wavelength-dependent: the scattering intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength (1/λ⁴)
- Blue light has a shorter wavelength (~450nm) than red light (~650nm)
- So blue light is scattered much more strongly than red light
- This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions, making the sky appear blue

2. Why does the sky turn red at sunset?
- At sunset, the sun is near the horizon
- Sunlight has to travel through a much thicker layer of atmosphere compared to when the sun is overhead
- Because of the longer path, more of the blue and green light is scattered away
- The remaining light that reaches our eyes is dominated by longer wavelengths (red, orange)
- This makes the sun and sky appear red/orange
